blocks.text: This chapter teaches the fundamentals of Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) in Python: classes and objects that model real-world entities in code, encapsulation that protects data, inheritance that lets code be reused and extended, and polymorphism that makes programs flexible. Together these help in writing well-structured, maintainable and scalable Python applications.

blocks.title: Object-Oriented Programming
blocks.text: Object-Oriented Programming is a way of designing programs using objects and classes. Each object represents a real-world entity with its own properties and behaviours, and classes are templates for creating many objects with similar characteristics.
OOP emphasises encapsulation, inheritance and polymorphism to manage data and behaviour efficiently, which helps in modelling real-world problems in programs.
Benefits of OOP: modularity, reusability and easier maintenance

items: Modularity: code is divided into modules (classes), which makes it easier to manage.
Reusability: classes and objects can be reused in many programs or parts of a program, reducing repetition.
Easier maintenance: a change in one part does not affect the whole system, so programs are easier to update.
Scalability and teamwork: the structure lets software grow and adapt, and organised, understandable code helps collaboration.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: Object-Oriented Programming helps programmers think in terms of real-life objects, like students or cars, which makes programs easier to understand and manage.

blocks.prompt: What is Object-Oriented Programming, and what are two of its benefits?
blocks.explanation: OOP designs programs with classes and objects that model real-world entities. Benefits include modularity (code split into manageable classes) and reusability (classes reused instead of rewriting code); maintenance is also easier.

items: OOP: programs built from classes (templates) and objects (real-world entities).
Benefits: modularity, reusability, easier maintenance, scalability.
